To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PbS QDs in combination with polymer-fullerene blends are a promising strategy to create tandem solar cells with broad spectral absorption; (2) The VOC of the tandem can be increased by using Al/WO3 as an interlayer; (3) A power conversion efficiency of up to 1.8% is obtained.
we demonstrate the first hybrid tandem cell with solution processability, and that we identify PbS QDs as a promising absorber for the front subcell.

(1) we report the first hybrid inorganic-organic solar cell using solution processable active layer materials, (2) we demonstrate the potential of combining PbS QD with small-bandgap organic semiconductors in hybrid tandem solar cells for the broad absorption of the entire solar spectrum, and (3) we show that an Al/WO3 interlayer can be used to obtain an open circuit voltage of about 92% the sum of the open circuit voltages of the subcells

the development of hybrid tandem solar cells for efficient conversion of the solar spectrum.
the design of hybrid tandem solar cells based on solution processable active materials for low cost photovoltaic applications.

the tandem cell is an interesting approach for the realization of highly efficient solar cells.
the combination of PbS QDs and small band gap polymers is very promising and should be further pursued.

this work demonstrates the first hybrid tandem cell with solution processible materials and that the combination of PbS QDs and small-bandgap polymeric semiconductors is promising for the future design of tandem solar cells with very broad absorption range, high short-circuit current and high open circuit voltage.

hybrid tandem solar cells are feasible and can reach a high efficiency.
we have shown that the tandem concept can be extended to hybrid solar cells with solution processable absorber layers.

we have demonstrated the first tandem solar cell with a PbS QD based front subcell and a polymer-fullerere rear subcell, and we have shown that this combination is a promising strategy for broad bandgap tandem solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of QDs with small bandgap polymers can be used to achieve tandem solar cells with broad absorption of the visible spectrum.

solution processable tandem cells can be made with a very broad spectral range by combining PbS QD and polymer-fullerene subcells, and that a significant fraction of the sum VOC can be obtained by introducing an interlayer between the two cells.
